title: Long-Time Dynamics
intro: Analyze communicating classes, periods, stationary laws and absorption for the current experiment. Initial-state changes update the mixture; stationary structure is cached independently.
timing: Label-law time starts at t = {{start}}. The horizon adds {{steps}} Markov transitions. Cesàro averages include every label law from t = {{start}} through the displayed time.
ordinary: Every recurrent class reachable from this initial law is aperiodic. The analyzed Markov chain converges to the displayed absorption mixture. The quantum mean follows when the analyzed transition matrix represents the model.
periodic: A reachable recurrent class is periodic (periods: {{periods}}). Ordinary convergence is not guaranteed for arbitrary inputs. Stationary inputs can still be constant. Cesàro averages of the analyzed chain converge to the displayed mixture.
multiple: There are {{count}} closed classes. Every stationary law is a convex combination of their stationary distributions. The initial law selects the mixture through absorption probabilities.
transientHelp: Transient states eventually enter a closed class. The weights below include their entire initial mass through aⱼ = q_start · hⱼ.
edgeInterpretation: An edge label indexes the pure scattered state U|xy⟩. Its invariant state measure and mixed barycenter are different objects. An individual instantaneous edge trajectory does not converge to the maximally mixed state. A single path's time average belongs to its selected recurrent class.
vertexInterpretation: A label indexes χ(x); the invariant quantum-state measure is the pushforward of the stationary label law. Different labels can prepare identical states. One path selects a recurrent class; its empirical time average need not equal the ensemble mixture. Phase-sensitive states retain ω and β.
analyticSupport: Analytical support from exactly recognized built-in matrices and boundary vectors. The reported tiny residual entries are known zeros for these formulas.
numericalSupport: Support is numerical, not certified: entries at or below {{tolerance}} are excluded and retained rows are rescaled for class analysis. This can change infinite-time behavior if a tiny rate is genuine. Use cutoff 0 to retain every stored positive rate.
supportDetails: Discarded entries: {{count}} · maximum removed row mass: {{mass}} · maximum row L1 change: {{change}}. Evolution curves use the original probabilities; stationary references use the support-policy matrix.
graphEdgeHelp: Each node is a directed-edge atom (target, source), not an original graph vertex. Arrows follow retained Markov transitions. Color shows class; size shows the selected stationary weight. Dashed borders mark transient states.
graphVertexHelp: Each node is a preparation label. Arrows follow retained Markov transitions. Color shows class; size shows the selected stationary weight. Dashed borders mark transient states. Select a node to highlight outgoing transitions.
graphDescription: Interactive reduced Markov-state graph with communicating-class colors and highlighted outgoing transitions.
localGraph: For more than 80 states, the graph shows the selected state and its outgoing neighbors. Tables still cover the complete chain.
label: Markov state
rowConvention: P: source rows → destination columns; q_next = q @ P.
columnConvention: M: source columns → destination rows; q_next = M @ q. Structural algorithms explicitly use T = Mᵀ internally.
sparseMatrix: Dense matrices are shown up to dimension 64. Use the sparse outgoing-transition table and state selector for this larger chain.
referenceHelp: The reference for both charts is always the initial-state absorption mixture. These are ensemble label laws, not post-preparation Born probabilities or single-path occupation frequencies.
selectedState: State for transitions and probability chart
probabilityChart: Selected-state ordinary, Cesàro and stationary probabilities over physical time
distanceChart: Ordinary and Cesàro total variation distances to the initial-state stationary mixture
quantumHelp: Reconstructs Σₑ πₑ|ηₑ⟩⟨ηₑ| for Edge, or Σₓ πₓ|χ(x)⟩⟨χ(x)| for Vertex. This density matrix is the mean of an invariant measure, not an individual trajectory state. Dense inspection supports dimension ≤ 64.
densityCaption: Stationary mean density matrix in the physical quantum basis
legendTip: Double-click on legend to isolate one trace
